blocks.text: The desktop can use the profile-pinned scx and scx-loader Debian packages. Each package receives a local dpkg-sig _gpgorigin signature and is published through a signed APT source whose Release metadata covers the package hashes. APT verifies the signed source metadata; the embedded package signature is an additional package-level attestation. When the selected host profile opts in, scx_loader.service is enabled for automatic startup and launches the configured default through its D-Bus loader. sched_ext can replace the kernel's normal CPU scheduling policy at runtime. Help only documents the commands; it never starts, stops, or switches a scheduler.

items: The loader reads /etc/scx_loader/config.toml. The managed default scheduler is scx_rusty and its default mode is Auto; scx_rusty is the long-running general-purpose profile.

The scx_loader.service and scx.service are separate backends. The opted-in system profile enables scx_loader.service and disables scx.service, so only one backend owns sched_ext. Entering the DevOps shell requests an idempotent switch to scx_flash through scxctl.

The pinned scx-loader release advertises scx_beerland, scx_bpfland, scx_cake, scx_cosmos, scx_eevdf, scx_flash, scx_flow, scx_forge, scx_lavd, scx_mlfq, scx_pandemonium, scx_p2dq, scx_tickless, scx_rustland, and scx_rusty. scx_bore and scx_bored are not in this release; use scxctl list to inspect the installed loader instead of guessing a name.
The units have a sched_ext feature condition. A kernel without /sys/kernel/sched_ext stays on its normal scheduler instead of repeatedly failing at boot.

blocks.text:
systemctl status scx_loader.service --no-pager
/usr/bin/scxctl list
/usr/bin/scxctl get
journalctl -u scx_loader.service -b

Use the existing administrator authorization path before changing a scheduler. Read the active mode and recent service log first. If a scheduler is unstable, stop or disable scx_loader.service through the administrator workflow and allow the kernel's built-in scheduler to take over; do not delete the configuration or rebuild scheduler binaries from source.

Scheduler behavior depends on the installed kernel, the profile-pinned scx packages, and current workload. Keep the direct scx.service disabled while the loader is in use, retain service logs after a failure, and treat a failed or uncertain transition as requiring inspection before another attempt.
